terms.gloss: The creatures the game is fought with: the card type that has HP, attacks and a stage, occupies the Active spot or the Bench, and is what Knock Outs and Prize cards are counted against.
The unit everything in the game is made of: a printed piece that belongs to a deck, moves between zones, and carries the type, name and rules text that decide what it can do.
Put a card from your hand onto the field and let it take effect, which is how Pokemon reach the Bench and Trainer cards are used.
One contest between two players, from setup until a win condition is met. It is the scope an effect limited to once per game is measured against, and the unit a Game Loss is recorded for.
The face-down stack a player draws from, built to a fixed size before the event and subject to the cap on how many cards may share one name.
The cards a player holds, hidden from the opponent; the zone cards are played from and the one a mulligan or a forced shuffle reworks.
One of the cards set aside face down at setup. A Knock Out lets the attacking player claim one or more, and claiming the last of them wins the game.
The harm an attack does, counted in tens and tracked with counters on the Pokemon; reaching its HP total Knocks it Out.
Anything a card makes happen beyond plain attack damage, whether it resolves at once or keeps applying afterwards.
The title printed on a card. Effects that look for a particular card match on it, and the deck-building copy cap counts by it rather than by printing.
sections: tcg-What does and doesn’t count for a Pokémon’s name?

terms.gloss: How far up its Evolution line a Pokemon card sits, printed in the corner. Effects are routinely keyed to a particular one.
The unevolved starting point: a Pokemon that can be played straight from hand with nothing beneath it, and by extension the plain Energy that carries no extra rules text.
The card type covering Items, Supporters, Stadiums and Tools, played for its written effect rather than to battle.
One player's stretch of the game loop, from their draw through their actions to the checkup that closes it.
One of the two sides in a game, owning a deck, a hand, a Bench and a set of Prize cards.
The other player in the game, whose Pokemon you attack and whose Prize cards and board an effect may reach.
End the game in your favour by meeting a win condition: claiming your last Prize card, leaving the opponent with no Pokemon in play, or leaving them unable to draw.
